objective: Test the selected uncertain Stirling-to-Saltmarket father and the dependent 1506 alias-Smith identity without conflating the documentary men.

questions.question: Does the full 1506 instrument identify the alias-Smith purchaser with Saltmarket John or connect him to the Stirling predecessor?

targets.reason: Full kin, title, alias and witness wording could distinguish the proposed family from namesake or collateral alternatives.
targets.note: Catalogue abstract held; original/full instrument not inspected. Read capacities, boundaries and endorsements as well as kin terms.

research_state.last_test: The downloaded Munimenta Alme Universitatis Glasguensis volume I (Privileges and Property) was searched for Glasgw/Glasgu, Smith/Smyth aliases and the 1506 date. The combined personal index, printed pp.55–56 (PDF167–168), was visually checked. The located 1506 texts concern other instruments; the 28 April BL204 instrument was not located. Volumes II and III were not searched in full, and this does not prove that the charter was never printed. No father or identity rating changes. The full BL204/GUA16403 remains the useful test.
research_state.next_test: Read full BL204/GUA16403 (28 April 1506): alias, capacities, kin/title, property, witnesses and endorsements.
research_state.blocker: Catalogue abstract does not supply the discriminating full instrument; OCR and abstracts cannot establish manuscript absence.
research_state.reopen_when: The full 1506 instrument or another newly readable identifying family/title clause becomes available.
